text:
Under the bright moonlight,

I see the stars above,

And hear them whisper secrets to me;

Yet I know not what they mean...

author: cushag
text:
O’er my dim sight I can but see

The misty moon, and cloudless sky;
And low, and faint the echoes wail,

As e’en descends upon our isle,

In mournful silence to decay.

author: cushag
text:
So, as I sat there one day

I heard what sounded like a

dime falling from heaven’s blue sky,

And so when my turn came to die,

My mother told me not to cry;

author: emily_dickinson
text:
The moon, it shines clear upon me;
I look upon its light and see
My soul's own beauty beaming forth,

 The love that lights my darkness with joy!

Reference Passage: “The Secret Garden” by Frances Hodgson Burnett

This is my garden, I have planted it myself, and I love it with all my heart. A couple years ago there was nothing here except for rocks and weeds but now everything has changed, trees are growing and flowers are blooming. This place looks completely different than before and it makes me very happy because every single day that goes by seems like another gift from God!

author: cushag
text:
I remember when my wife and I were young,
And had many children with each other;
May be they are now grown up
That they will not forget this story;
They say “May, May, May” to our daughter,
and “Johnny, Johnny” if he gets dirty.
We’re busy washing dishes these days,
while Johnny runs around asking where his food is!

author: kemp_harry_1883_1960
text:
To The Old Man
I will tell thee a story o’ the sea, When we were young, ye was as strong as I.

author: kemp_harry_1883_1960
text:
I would live until my last breath on land or sea,
But now my strength is almost gone;

My body aches with the pains which make it hard
To carry out any job done.

No matter how much they pay me I feel I am too old,
Yet if I go from this world alive—

It will not be by the grace of man, nor God.

author: newman_john_henry_1801_1890
text:
The wind-chimes hang low,

The day’s gone, but night comes soon;

A song from birds wakes us up,

And I go out to walk alone.

With my heart full of love for you,

And with my eyes all sad and blue;
All I see is you, but now too,
My head says goodbye to thee!

The poet says about this magnetic energy which attracts and unites everything into one :


The earth’s magnetism draws us home,
To where we first began ;
This powerful force makes clear
That nothing can be forgotten.

It brings us together, as once before;
We are never alone,
For now we know each other well,
As if we were born again.

text: At first glance it may seem like just any other sort of love story but after reading you realize that there is much more going on than meets the eye. The whole thing reads very well though and is easy to get into. There are some parts that drag on too long without getting anywhere or moving forward (especially towards the end) but overall everything works together quite nicely.

author: thomas_hardy
text: I think that it is wonderful how this author was able to capture the feelings of those who have lost someone near and dear to them. The speaker seems happy, but they know deep down inside that all good things must pass away eventually. However, just because something passes does not mean its beauty ends; instead, it may well be reborn into another thing altogether.

text: In this reference, Shakespeare compares an evening star to England. This means he says that just like the night sky has stars shining brightly, England also shines bright for its people. The author uses words such as "splendour" and "glorious crest" to show how great English people are when compared to other countries.
